name: security-kerberos-delegation-scope-review
intent: Kerberos delegation configuration and service-to-service identity scope
artifacts: Account/SPN mapping, delegation settings, allowed targets and service authorization policy.
trace: Trace which service identity may act for which user toward which target, separating ticket issuance from accepted protected operations.
experiment: Use owned lab principals and a harmless test service, or perform configuration-only analysis when ticket testing is outside scope.
disproof: A delegation flag or SPN is not demonstrated arbitrary domain access; protected-user constraints and target policy may stop the path.
repair: Limit delegation to intended services/users and retest legitimate service flows and forbidden target selection.
branch_decisions: Distinguish unconstrained, traditional constrained and resource-based constrained delegation with actual account flags and service principals. A delegation setting is not proof the actor controls the delegating principal or can obtain a usable ticket. Trace the permitted service/identity transition from supplied configuration without capturing or replaying production tickets.
operational_method: Map actual mode artifacts: unconstrained delegation uses the TRUSTED_FOR_DELEGATION account flag; traditional constrained delegation uses the service account msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo SPN list, with protocol-transition prerequisites such as TRUSTED_TO_AUTH_FOR_DELEGATION where applicable. Resource-based constrained delegation instead uses the target msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity security descriptor. Do not impose one mode flag on every other mode. Retain protected/nondelegable-user restrictions, principal/SPN mapping and authority to edit the controlling object. Trace supplied configuration to KDC ticket issuance and final service authorization; a flag or ticket alone is not a protected action.
